contract: POST /api/api-keys lets an admin create a named key for an existing user: name must be a non-empty string, userId an existing user id, expiresIn when truthy must be a positive number (0 means no expiry), a non-root admin cannot target root, and the response returns the signed key plus the persisted projection; omitted isActive stores false.
exceptions: force is not applicable: this route has no force, hard or override mode

invariants.contract: A valid create answers 200 with {apiKey:{apiKey:<JWT>, id, name, expiresAt, userId, isActive, createdByUserId, createdAt, updatedAt, user:{id,username,type}}}, persists the row with the requested user/flag/expiry (expiresAt 3600s after creation for expiresIn 3600), allows repeated names as separate rows, and the JWT authenticates its bearer as the target user; omitted expiresIn and expiresIn 0 store a never-expiring inactive key whose token is rejected.

POST /api/api-keys answers 400 for a missing or non-string name, a non-positive or non-numeric expiresIn, a missing/non-string/unknown userId, 403 when a non-root admin targets root and 401 without a token; every rejection adds no row.
